one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14 are the main scheduled event in the window. Q3 guidance is EUR 11.0-12.0B sales at 55-57% gross margin, and the FY26 guide of EUR 43-45B (H1 EUR 18.09B) implies Q4 of about EUR 14.4B. I expect ASML to give its first qualitative 2027 view on the call. The Q2 transcript supports a constructive one: low-NA EUV for 2027 is 'close to being fully covered with orders', capacity rises about 30% to roughly 85 units, and the E/F tool mix lifts wafer capacity about 45%. Customer read-across in the window is also strong. Micron (2026-09-30) guided FQ1-27 revenue to $61.5B, said supply would tighten further in 2027-28 and raised capex. TrendForce (2026-09-30) sees DRAM contract prices up 15-20% in Q4 including HBM. Three things argue against a confident upside call. Consensus 2027 EPS has already risen from about 41.5 to 51.7. The stock has rebounded about 15% from $1,575 on 2026-09-14, a 7% one-day fall caused by AI-slowdown sentiment rather than fundamentals (TIKR). And MATCH Act or US-Dutch export-control headlines can land at any time: the Dutch PM said on 2026-09-24/25 that he expects a deal, while NDAA conference action usually comes later, in Nov-Dec. Net bookings are no longer disclosed, which removes one source of surprise. I keep the distribution near symmetric with the median nudged up to about $1,818. Sigma is 14%, a little above the plain monthly 13% (46%/3.5), because of the earnings event.

fair_value.method: This is a 60/40 blend of two methods. The first is a forward P/E: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of EUR 58.7 ($66.0) x 28 = $1,848. The second is a 2028E FCF yield: FCF/share of EUR 58.0 at a 3.25% yield = EUR 1,785, or $2,007. Both convert at EUR/USD 1.1245. The 2028E EPS of EUR 61 already includes a probability-weighted haircut of about 4% for the MATCH Act.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 = 0.25 x 2027E EUR 51.7 + 0.75 x 2028E EUR 61.0 = EUR 58.7 = $66.0 at 1.1245; x 28 forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Spread consensus of EUR 51.72, up from about 41.5 ninety days earlier. I cross-checked it against the Q2 transcript: about 30% more low-NA units (roughly 65 to 85) with an E/F mix worth about 45% more wafer capacity, plus memory and installed-base growth, makes EUR 51.7 look reachable rather than stretched (sources 2, 11).

H1 reported EPS is EUR 14.74. Q3 at the guidance midpoint (EUR 11.5B x 56% GM, less about EUR 1.6B opex, 17% tax, about 384M shares) gives about EUR 10.5. The implied Q4 of about EUR 14.4B gives about EUR 13.9. The total is about EUR 39.

Gross EUR 63.5 (+23% on 2027 consensus). Management is investigating a further ~30% capacity step for 2028 and already holds 'a significant number' of 2028 low-NA orders. TSMC says capex over the next three years will be 'even more significantly higher' than the past three. Micron expects supply to tighten further through 2027-28. Pricing flexibility and the EUR 12B buyback add a little. From the gross figure I take a probability-weighted 4% haircut for the MATCH Act. That act (S.4281, riding the Senate NDAA) would ban immersion DUV sales to China and servicing at five named Chinese fabs, against China at about 20% of sales. I assume about a 40% chance of enactment in a binding form and about a 10% EPS hit if enacted. The Dutch PM's 2026-09-25 push for a negotiated deal keeps the probability below 50%.

Today the stock trades at about 33x a blended NTM EPS of about EUR 48.5 (EUR 1,608 = $1,808.49 / 1.1245). Torre Financial puts it at 23.6x NTM EBITDA against a 10-year mean of 24.9x, so it is not extreme against its own history. In Oct-2027 the market will be looking at decelerating growth after the 2027 step-up, so I apply a moderate de-rating to 28x, the middle of ASML's mid-20s to mid-30s forward range.
Twelve Data spot of 1.1243-1.1247 on 2026-10-01/02; 1 ADR = 1 ordinary share

The 20-F shows FY25 FCF of EUR 11.0B on net income of EUR 9.6B (115%) and FY24 FCF of EUR 9.1B on EUR 7.6B (about 120%). Contract liabilities (customer down payments) were EUR 18.2B at YE25 (EUR 12.6B current plus EUR 5.6B non-current). H1-26 FCF, however, was about -EUR 1.3B (OCF -EUR 0.48B, capex and intangibles EUR 0.81B) because receivables rose by about EUR 4.2B into the ramp, and capacity capex is rising. I therefore use 95%, below the FY24-25 average but above my earlier 90%.
Same as in the P/E method

Torre Financial gives today's trailing FCF yield as 1.8% against a 10-year average of 2.6%. A 2028E (two-year-forward) yield of 3.25% equals roughly 2.7% on NTM FCF in Oct-2027, i.e. a return to the 10-year average with no premium for peak growth.

bear.story: This case is a combination of the following. The MATCH Act passes in the FY27 NDAA without a Dutch carve-out, removing immersion DUV sales and servicing at five Chinese fabs (part of the about 20% China share). The market decides 2027 is the peak as memory pricing moderates in H2-27 (TrendForce already sees slowing increases) or AI capex digests; the 2026-09-14 one-day fall of 7% on an essay shows how sentiment-sensitive the stock is. Gross margin also stalls around 54-55%. The stock de-rates to about 21x a trimmed 2027 EPS of about EUR 50.

base.story: 2027 delivers about 85 low-NA units on the E/F mix, with sales of roughly EUR 54-57B and EPS of about EUR 52. The June 2027 CMD confirms the 2028 capacity step and raises the 2030 framework above EUR 44-60B. The China export-control outcome is a negotiated, narrower Dutch-US arrangement. The multiple compresses to about 28x NTM EPS of about EUR 59.

bull.story: Customers keep pulling forward: TSMC capex accelerates toward analyst estimates of about $77B for 2027, Micron's and SK hynix's further capacity adds land in 2028, and ASML confirms 110+ low-NA units of capacity for 2028 with better pricing. High-NA availability reaches 90% and orders follow (TSMC committed to volume use around 2030). The multiple holds at about 32x on 2028 EPS of about EUR 66.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $1,150 the stock trades at roughly 20x consensus 2027 EPS (EUR 51.7, about $58) and below its 2026-09-14 panic low of $1,575 by more than a quarter. That level would most likely mean an absolute cut to 2027 shipments or order deferrals, for example customers pushing out EUV slots or a TSMC, Samsung or hyperscaler capex freeze, or a MATCH-style enactment that also hits the China installed base. Either would contradict management's 'close to fully covered' 2027 order book rather than being ordinary 46%-vol noise.

reasoning: This continuation redoes round 1 with the uncapped search budget. The primary documents still show strong acceleration. Q2-26 sales were EUR 9.3B at 54.0% GM, the FY26 guide is EUR 43-45B, the implied Q4 is about EUR 14.4B, there are about 65 low-NA units in 2026 rising to about 85 in 2027 on an E/F mix (+45% wafer capacity), 2028 orders are already significant, and management sees pricing flexibility. New primary checks: (1) The 20-F shows FCF conversion above 100% in FY24-25 and contract liabilities of EUR 18.2B at YE25. My round-1 figure of EUR 3.6B was only the non-current piece, which corrects that fact. It also shows customer concentration of 23.9% for the largest customer and 38% for the top two. (2) The Q2 cash-flow statement shows H1-26 FCF of about -EUR 1.3B from a receivables build. (3) Customer primary documents point to rising lithography demand: TSMC raised 2026 capex to $60-64B and expects 'even more significantly higher' spending over three years, and Micron guided record FQ1-27 and higher capex. (4) The new bear evidence is the MATCH Act (S.4281), which would ban immersion DUV sales to China and servicing at five fabs and is riding the Senate NDAA. Against that, the Dutch PM expects a deal (2026-09-25). I added a probability-weighted 4% EPS haircut and put enactment into the bear case. Sentiment fragility is evident from the 2026-09-14 one-day fall of 7%. The fair value rises from $1,842 to about $1,912, mainly through better-evidenced FCF conversion and a yield anchored to the 10-year average, partly offset by the MATCH haircut. That is about 6% above spot. Analyst targets, used as evidence only: Alpha Spread mean EUR 2,098; Morgan Stanley cut to EUR 1,700 on 2026-09-08 on China and margin worries. The ladder is a mixture. The main mode (77%) has a median of $2,010 and sigma of 0.33. A bear mode (23%) has a median of $1,250 and sigma of 0.30, covering export-control enactment or a cycle-top de-rating; semicap stocks have historically fallen 40-50% in such episodes. The result is P(>= today) of about 0.51, a mean of about $1,935 (about +7%), and an overall width consistent with 46% realised volatility. Remaining gaps: Twelve Data estimate endpoints need a higher plan, ASML's own financial-calendar page returned 503 (the CMD date comes from ASML's investors page via search), and no prediction market on the MATCH Act was found.
